missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Мороз' is masculine and stays in the nominative as the subject. 'Сильный' is the agreeing masculine adjective, and 'на улице' gives the location.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Мороз' is inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative as the object of 'люблю'. 'Зимний' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Мороза' is the genitive form after 'нет', stating that there is no hard frost today. 'Сильного' agrees in the masculine genitive.
Strategic focus: Instrumental of means. 'Морозом' takes the instrumental, naming what covers the trees. 'Белым' agrees in the masculine instrumental, completing the wintry image.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Морозе' takes the prepositional after 'при', meaning during the frost. 'Сильном' agrees in the masculine prepositional.
Strategic focus: Dative complement. 'Морозу' takes the dative after the short adjective 'рады', which governs that case. 'Первому' agrees in the masculine dative.
Strategic focus: Genitive after preposition. 'Мороза' takes the genitive after 'из-за', giving the cause of the difficulty. 'Трудно дышать' states the effect of the cold.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Морозы' is the nominative plural subject of 'бывают'. 'Крепкие' agrees in the plural, and 'зимой' sets the season.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural of fear. 'Морозов' is the genitive plural required by 'боимся', which governs the genitive. 'Ночных' agrees in the genitive plural.
Strategic focus: Genitive after preposition. 'Мороза' takes the genitive after 'после', placing the thaw in time. 'Наступила' marks the change of weather.
